$comment: The source of sf-chat-interlocutor's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.9, vocabulary 1.1.5. Moved from simai/ui-chat components/src/smart/chat-interlocutor (smart.manifest.json 0.3.1, ui-chat 10d376b) by the D31 move, step 3 (owner yes 2026-10-27); written by hand on the shape of sf-change-confirm and sf-thread-list, since migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs takes only the pinned 66 and needs stand 17's output. x-decisions says how each point was decided.

options.x-markup: a property (a host has objects), or the JSON island a server prints; kind knowledge goes under its own heading after the person's own; title is text, never markup. setOptions(list), the 0.3 call, is the action set-options

value.summary: the current interlocutor; a choice asks for another with select {id} and the host writes it back when its new conversation is there

select.x-summary: Another interlocutor was chosen (vocabulary §5 select, one id as sf-context-menu's select carries). A conversation belongs to one interlocutor, so the host starts a new one and writes value back; the element never changes value itself.

set-options.x-summary: the interlocutors the server lists (bootstrap.interlocutors), as the setting options; the 0.3 setOptions(list)

open.x-summary: opens the choice (the button's press); refused single with fewer than two interlocutors, where there is nothing to choose

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16).

accessibility.x-keys: Enter and Space press the native button, which opens sf-context-menu; inside it the menu's own keys (arrows, Home, End, letters, Escape); with one interlocutor the button is disabled and no key does anything

x-summary: Who the conversation is with: the server's interlocutors in the Framework's context menu, the current one checked, and a choice of another reported for the host to start a new conversation with. One interlocutor is a name, not a choice.

x-source.converted: by hand (D31 step 3): convert-1.3.8.mjs reads stand 17's output, which has no chat component

x-renamed: events.sf-chat-interlocutor → select {id} (vocabulary §5 select; an event takes its tag and a verb, §7); the old name a dated same-detail alias until 2026-12-01
methods.setOptions(list) → the setting options and the action set-options {options} (§4.4); setOptions(list) is the same call, so nothing is noted

words: interlocutor.* and assistant of ui-chat's strings.js → lang/<locale>.json runtime words (§11): assistant-text, button-label, menu-label, change-text, search-placeholder, search-empty-text, group-own-text, group-knowledge-text

css: --sf-chat--ink, --sf-chat--ink-muted and --sf-chat--touch of ui-chat's chat.css → the Framework tokens they were, under five public variables --sf-chat-interlocutor-<name>; .sf-chat-offscreen → the Framework's sr-only

forbidden_client_responsibilities: fetching or polling the chat API

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-chat-interlocutor in a chat window's header to name whom the conversation is with and, when the server lists several, to let the person choose another one, which the host turns into a new conversation.
do_not: Do not set value from the select event before the host has its new conversation; write it back when it does
Do not use it to pick a conversation: that is sf-thread-list's open
Do not pass markup in titles; they are text

x-decisions: version: 0.3.1 in simai/ui-chat → 1.0.0 here: the first release in ui-pro, a new tag in the open sf- set (§21.4), with the event renamed under a dated alias (simai.linkage 1.0.0: the files changed).

shape: a leaf, a thin element over the Framework's sf-context-menu (D31 inventory §3: interlocutor and sf-thread-list rows do not overlap). It places one native button, an sf-icon and the menu as its own markup; no part is in a role a rule could bind.

events: the 0.3 sf-chat-interlocutor {id} is the vocabulary's select (§5): the person chose; the host decides what it means (a new conversation). It carries {id}, one id as sf-context-menu's own select does, not {ids}: a conversation has one interlocutor. Cancelable as it was. The old name follows as a same-detail alias until 2026-12-01; a page that cancels either keeps nothing to undo, the element changed nothing.
value: a controlled value (as sf-thread-list's selected): the element shows it and never writes it; the host writes it back once its conversation is with the new interlocutor.

options and set-options: the list is the setting options (a property, or the JSON island of §5.4); the 0.3 method setOptions(list) is the action set-options {options}, which the generated method takes in declared order, so the 0.3 call is the same call.

single: fewer than two interlocutors is a name, not a choice: the button is disabled, without aria-haspopup, aria-expanded and the description, the chevron hidden (class sf-chat-interlocutor--single), and open answers refused single.

former interlocutor: a value the options no longer list (Mirai24 v1.1: the administrator's assistant gone into the personal one, its old threads kept) is named by the word assistant-text («Помощник»), never by an empty line; an empty value with no options is an empty name.

menu: radio rows, the current one checked; the person's own interlocutors first, then kind knowledge under group headings when both are there; from eight the menu has its search (SEARCH_FROM, as in 0.3); a closing heading says a change starts a new conversation.

a11y-name: the button reads «Помощник: <title>» (button-label) when the current interlocutor is listed, else its title alone; its description (sr-only, id from the instance path §7.1.1, no longer a module counter) says a change starts a new conversation, before the menu opens (ui-chat Q-08); aria-expanded is false from the start (Q-09) and the menu keeps it after.

first paint (§5.4): no late data. The options come with the host's bootstrap, together with value; the printed markup is the closed button (a closed menu is printed closed: the trigger). A host that loads its interlocutors later holds its own skeleton (sf-chat-window). The element reads no clock, so its snapshots do not depend on the fixed clock of the first-paint tools (ui-source 4d711d2), which the pinned 170d551 does not have yet.
words: lang/ru.json and lang/en.json, runtime only; ru is the source language (the 0.3 words were written in Russian first).

css-variables: five public variables in the Framework's form (single dash, read with the token as fallback, never set): the text, the chevron, the hover ground, the corner and the height (a finger's on a coarse pointer). Their fallbacks are the tokens ui-chat's chat.css gave the same places, so the look in ui-chat does not change.

self-contained: nothing from simai/ui-chat is imported; the chat-core base (ChatElement, staffContext) is replaced by the Framework's Smart base through elementFromManifest and the element's own words.
